rows.title: Principles of Accounting II
rows.title_printed: Course Outline: Riverside Community College District
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to demonstrate the following skills:
outcomes: Solve problems, analyze, explain, and apply managerial accounting principles to manufacturing and service enterprises.
Recognize the role of ethics in managerial accounting.
Identify, use, and appropriately apply managerial accounting terminology.
Students will develop the ability to evaluate diverse perspectives and discuss the complexity of differing viewpoints as they relate to the accounting profession in an equity-based environment.
objectives: Explain why ethics are crucial to accounting and identify ethical implications inherent in managerial accounting and recognize strategies for addressing ethical issues.
Describe the role of the Institute of Management Accountants and the use of ethical standards.
Identify managerial accounting vocabulary with corresponding definitions and explain managerial accounting concepts and principals.
Explain the differences between managerial and financial accounting including timing, users of reports, and GAAP requirements.
Describe the nature of manufacturing operations and identify cost classifications.
Identify the key differences between a service company and a manufacturer’s financial statements with respect to the income statement and balance sheet.
Illustrate and apply cost flow schedules for direct materials, work in process, and finished goods manufacturing inventory accounts.

Compare and contrast different costing systems and distinguish key differences with respect to job order costing, process costing and activity-based costing, to track and allocate total manufacturing costs and prepare managerial reports based on each system.
Calculate predetermined overhead rates using various methods to allocate overhead costs to products.
Distinguish between variable costs, fixed costs, and mixed costs by understanding their relationship when computing contribution margins, performing break-even analysis, or achieving target profit.
Apply transactional analysis and input transactions into an accounting system; process this input and its relationship to the financial statements of a manufacturing environment.
Discuss support department and joint cost allocation and apply methods for calculating overhead costs.
Apply cost-volume-profit analysis to understand the relationships between cost, volume, and profit, including how this impacts management’s decision-making.
Identify and illustrate the difference between absorption costing and variable costing with regards to changes in operating income when units sold does not equal units produced.
Describe how absorption costing is used by management to understand the impact of variable and fixed expenses on market segments.
Recognize types of budgets, know their importance, and understand the elements of the budget process by constructing operational and financial budgets for a manufacturing company.
Describe and identify budget and operational performance measures and calculate manufacturing variances affecting labor, materials, and overhead costs.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of decentralized operations and prepare evaluations.
Identify and apply responsibility accounting for profit, cost, and investment centers.
Explain differential analysis and its importance to managerial decisions and its impact on profitability.
Explain the importance of capital investment analysis and use capital investment methods for evaluating long-term investments.
Identify how lean manufacturing practices impact the accounting systems of businesses.
Explain how the balanced score card and corporate social responsibility impacts business objectives and promotes sustainability.

rows.title: African American History II
rows.title_printed: Course Outline: Riverside Community College District
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to demonstrate the following skills:
outcomes: Demonstrate active engagement with anti-racist issues, practices and movements to build a diverse, just and equitable society beyond the classroom as well as demonstrate the ability to think independently, review and analyze information reflectively, and reason logically based on review and interpretation of historical information.

Describe how struggle, resistance, social justice solidarity and liberation as experienced by African Americans are relevant to current issues and reflect upon contemporary concerns of, and issues regarding, African Americans in a global context and based on an understanding of US history.

Critically discuss the intersection of race and ethnicity with other forms of difference affected by hierarchy and oppression, such as class, gender, sexuality, religion, spirituality, national origin, immigration status, ability and/or age and be able to explain and interpret the laws created and implemented to enslave African people and the subsequent legacy of those laws on the status and identity of African Americans and the implications of those laws for all of American society.

Apply theory to describe critical events in the histories, cultures, and intellectual traditions, with special focus on the lived-experiences and social struggles of African Americans emphasizing agency and group-affirmation.

Analyze and articulate concepts of ethnic studies, including but not limited to race and ethnicity, racialization, equity, ethno-centrism, eurocentrism, white supremacy, self-determination, liberation, decolonization, and anti-racism.
objectives: Identify the ways that freed African Americans dealt with economic and social change, including employment and education.
Describe the role of the Freedmen’s Bureau in the Reconstruction period.
Explain the role of the black church in the creation of community and political leaders.
Describe the reaction of white Americans to the end of the war, including violence and black codes.
Analyze how Congress and President Johnson influenced Reconstruction through the Reconstruction Acts.
Explain how the Thirteenth and Fourteenth amendments affected the African-American community.
Describe segregation and how the Plessy v. Ferguson decision contributed to it.
Explain the role that violence played in the lives of African Americans, including race riots and lynching.
Analyze the reasons behind the migration of African Americans to Africa, the western United States, and Southern
cities, and the effects of that migration.
Express how the justice system has historically been applied to African Americans.
Compare and contrast the two philosophies of African-American progress, represented by Booker T. Washington and W.E.B. DuBois.
Explain the role of African-American soldiers in the U.S. Armed Forces from the Civil War to World War I.
Describe the reasons behind the Great Migration.
Explain the roots of the Harlem Renaissance and the Jazz Age and identify a few of the major artists associated with it.
Describe the reasons behind the resurrection of the Ku Klux Klan and the changes in the organization during the 1920s.
Explain some of the causes of the Great Depression and why African Americans were heavily impacted.
Describe the steps the NAACP took during the 1930s to challenge racial inequality in schools.
Analyze how President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s First New Deal affected African Americans.
Explain how Brown vs. the Board of Education of Topeka, Kansas, changed the face of segregation.
Analyze the Little Rock desegregation challenge and how it reflected the white backlash to the progress of African Americans.
Describe a few of the grassroots efforts toward progress, including sit-ins, freedom rides, and the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC).
Discuss how the legal changes in the 1960s offered more opportunities for African Americans.
Analyze how the black power and black nationalism grew out of the civil rights movement and the reasons behind urban violence during the late 1960s.
Trace the development of an increased political voice of African Americans from the local to the national level, including those who ran for president.
Identify how No Child Left Behind, the Welfare Reform Act, and affirmative action affects the lives of African Americans.
Analyze the ways in which African Americans have not yet reached economic equality with white Americans.
Explain how incarceration and police brutality continue to be an important issue in the African-American community and the nation at large.
Discuss the challenges and divisions exposed by the 2016 election, the Obama presidency, and the Trump era, along with the protests and reactions that occurred afterward.

rows.title: Historical Geology
rows.title_printed: Course Outline: Riverside Community College District
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to demonstrate the following skills:
outcomes: Describe the scientifically accepted ideas concerning the formational processes of the earth and the processes and characteristics of plate tectonics.
Summarize the scientifically accepted ideas concerning the formation and evolution of life through time and the evidence of that life as viewed through fossils and fossil assemblages.
Explain the geologic time scale and general characteristics of life during each geologic time period.
Describe the many ways biologic materials and animal behaviors are preserved in the fossil record through the formation of both body and trace fossils.

Demonstrate an understanding of the impact geological forces and plate tectonics can have on animals and how organisms have responded to the evolution of the Earth's oceans and the distribution of landmasses through time.
objectives: Use the scientific method to address and answer questions posed in lecture and lab.
Describe the scientifically accepted ideas of the formation of the Solar System, the Earth and the moon.
Describe the theory of Plate Tectonics, the evidence supporting it, the types of plate boundaries and the physiographic features created by plate tectonic activity.
Summarize the processes of the formation of both plutonic and volcanic igneous rock and provide examples of where different types may be found.
Explain the agents, textures and parent materials of metamorphic rocks and describe what the index minerals tell us of the geologic history of a region.
Explain the many ways sedimentary rocks may form, the environments in which they form and what information the rocks provide about those environments.
Use the facies concept and Walther's Law to interpret shifting depositional environments through time and make sequence stratigraphic interpretations from outcrop studies.
Use the principles of relative dating and biostratigraphy to interpret a rock sequence.
Use absolute dating calculations to age date rocks from mass spectrometer data sets.
Discuss the scientifically accepted ideas concerning the origins of life and evolution of life through time.
Recognize and explain the different modes of fossilization, the types of materials typically preserved and the requirements for preservation to occur.
Analyze the data available from both body fossils and trace fossils to interpret the geologic and faunal history of a region.
Prepare cladograms to examine evolutionary relationships between different groups of animals.
Examine and evaluate the evidence for events in the Proterozoic such as evolution of the planet's atmosphere, the Snowball Earth hypothesis, life in the Proterozoic and the Ediacaran Fauna.
Describe events in the Mesozoic such as the breakup of Pangea, growth of epicontinental seas, the rise and evolution of dinosaurs, development of birds, and the evolution of Mammals.
Examine and analyze the data available for the big five mass extinction events in order to assess possible causes and the ecological outcomes.
Describe events in the Cenozoic such as major phases of mountain building, the ice ages, the evolution of mammals and mega fauna, and human evolution.

Analyze the construction of “race” and its relationship to the formation of the institution of American slavery.
Examine the various interactions of African-descended Americans with other groups in colonial America and the United States.
Display knowledge of African-centered worldviews and their role in the psychological study of people of African descent.
Analyze the intellectual, philosophical, and cultural developments of African American experience.
Identify theoretical frameworks in the field of African American studies.

rows.lead: Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to demonstrate the following skills:
outcomes: Provide quality, safe, patient-centered care as designed by the state-mandated theory and clinical modules.
Demonstrate appropriate ethical, legal and professional principles while implementing the Nursing Assistant (NA) role.
Perform the duties of the certified nursing assistant under the leadership of a licensed vocational or registered nurse.
Demonstrate caring behaviors through nursing assistant skills that positively influence health outcomes and displays sensitivity to the values of others.
Maintain collaborative relationships with other members of the healthcare team.
Begin to use critical thinking principles to recognize and report impending emergencies in the role of the nursing assistant.
Utilize technology to perform designated tasks and skills.
objectives: Describe the role and responsibilities of Nursing Assistants (NAs) in the delivery of healthcare in various settings and demonstrate competence in performing the role of a NA in the long-term care setting.
Explain the obligations and role of NAs in maintaining resident rights and demonstrate this understanding as an advocate for assigned residents in the clinical setting.
Describe influencing factors that affect communication in healthcare settings and use effective communication skills in the clinical setting.
State principles of body mechanics, give examples of effective use in healthcare settings, and demonstrate principles of body mechanics when providing care as assigned.
Discuss principles and practices of medical and surgical asepsis and apply these practices appropriately when providing care.
Compare the use of selected systems of measurement used in healthcare settings and demonstrate competency in using clinical measurement systems.
Identify methods for accurately obtaining, measuring, and recording vital signs accurately in the clinical setting.
Describe methods for performing basic patient care skills and procedures using identified resources in a safe and competent manner.

Describe the relationship between nutrition and health status, giving specific examples relevant to residents in long-term care settings, and demonstrate competency in feeding residents and assisting residents with meals.

Recognize signs and symptoms of impending emergencies, and identify and initiate appropriate immediate and temporary interventions certified nursing assistants should implement in selected situations.
Describe the basic needs in promoting the restoration of health for residents commonly cared for in long-term settings.

Describe the stages of death and dying and the grieving process, giving examples of how to assist residents and their support persons at various stages, and appropriately assist assigned residents and their support persons in the clinical setting.
Articulate principles of safety, infection control, and emotional, spiritual, and social needs of patients.

rows.title: Nursing Learning Laboratory
rows.title_printed: Course Outline: Riverside Community College District
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to demonstrate the following skills:
outcomes: At the beginner novice level: Provide quality, safe, patient-centered nursing care at a foundational level using evidence-based practices for individuals and families across the lifespan.
Identify the scope and standards of practice of the professional nurse generalist, including a foundational understanding of ethical and legal principles in health care.
Recognize leadership principles in select health care settings for diverse patient populations.
Identify caring behaviors that support relationship-centered care and demonstrate respect and sensitivity to others in preparation for becoming a competent, entry-level professional nurse generalist.

Identify the role of the registered nurse in collaborative relationships using effective communication with the interprofessional health care team, at a foundational level, for the purpose of providing & improving patient outcomes.
Demonstrate foundational principles of critical thinking that begin to develop clinical reasoning and judgment necessary for providing safe patient care and promoting quality improvement.

Understand the principles of nursing informatics and the use of technology to effectively communicate, enhance knowledge, manage and analyze data, prevent errors, and support decision-making in preparation for becoming a competent, entry-level professional nurse generalist.
objectives: At a beginner novice level: Quality, Safe, Patient-Centered Care A. Develop a patient-centered plan of care, using the nursing process, that addresses the psychosocial and physiological needs of the patient within the health care system. B. Perform and document a fundamental assessment for patients across the lifespan encompassing values, preferences, expressed needs, and the impact of developmental, emotional, cultural, religious, and spiritual influences on the patient’s health status. C. Select and incorporate patient-centered interventions that demonstrate sensitivity and respect for the diversity of the human experience. D. Identify and incorporate evidence-based practices to guide clinical decision-making in the delivery of quality, safe nursing care. E. Safely perform fundamental psychomotor nursing skills within the context of the patient situation. F. Safely prepare and administer medications, including the accurate calculation of drug dosages. G. Incorporate patient-centered teaching interventions into the delivery of nursing care. H. Demonstrate patient advocacy skills in the care of assigned patients and their families.

Ethical and Legal Principles: A. Understand and demonstrate professional standards, ethical behaviors, and legal principles of nursing practice. B. Establish professional attitudes and behaviors, including attention to appearance, demeanor, respect for self and others, and attention to professional boundaries with patients and families as well as caregivers. C. Develop a nursing philosophy statement that includes an individualized plan for lifelong learning in preparation for becoming a professional nurse generalist.

Leadership Principles: A. Develop and use organizational and time management skills to safely manage the health care needs of assigned patients. B. Recognize the leadership roles of the professional nurse in health care settings. C. Demonstrate accountability and responsibility for nursing care provided and identify situations when care can be delegated to other members of the health care team. D. Identify quality improvement principles and practices used in the health care setting and how they contribute to improving patient outcomes.

Caring: A. Involve the patient and family when planning or providing patient-centered care. B. Select nursing interventions appropriate to the patient’s developmental level; physical and psychological needs; spiritual beliefs; and culture. C. Identify and develop expected patient outcomes in a collaborative and caring manner that provides direction for continuity of care. D. Demonstrate relationship-centered care principles when caring for self and interacting with patients, families, peers, and other members of the health care team.

Collaborative Relationships: A. Demonstrate effective communication techniques to foster positive professional working relationships. B. Recognize the role of the registered nurse in fostering collaborative relationships with the health care team in improving patient outcomes. C. Use effective communication and collaborative skills with the health care team to deliver evidence-based patient-centered care. D. Select interventions that promote quality, safe patient-centered care as a member of the health care team that contribute to improving patient care outcomes. E. Use and document basic patient care data to inform the health care team and contribute to clinical decision-making. F. Identify and report relevant information to an appropriate health care team member to improve patient outcomes.

Critical Thinking: A. Use beginning clinical reasoning and judgment skills when providing quality, safe patient-centered care. B. Begin to collect data to assist in problem identification, goal attainment, and the selection of interventions based on the patient’s health care needs. C. Participate in guided self-reflection activities to identify professional learning needs. D. Use quality improvement principles to identify potential problems that may interfere with the delivery of safe patient care.

Nursing Informatics: A. Demonstrate basic computer literacy, including the ability to use desktop applications and mobile technology to promote communication and support decision-making. B. Establish foundational skills using patient care technologies, information systems, and communication devices that support safe nursing care. C. Use of information technology systems, at a foundational level, to prevent the risk of errors and improve clinical outcomes in the delivery of safe patient care. D. Begin to access data and document using the nursing process via electronic health record, abiding by all ethical and legal standards.

outcomes: At the intermediate novice level: Provide quality, safe, patient-centered nursing care using evidence-based practices for patients with acute and chronic alterations in health.

Assimilate the scope and standards of practice in preparation for becoming a competent, entry-level professional nurse generalist, applying ethical and legal principles when providing care for patients with acute and chronic alterations in health.

Model caring behaviors that support relationship-centered care and demonstrate respect and sensitivity to others in preparation for becoming a competent, entry-level professional nurse generalist.

Apply communication principles to foster collaborative relationships using effective communication with the interprofessional health care team for the purpose of providing and improving patient outcomes in preparation for becoming a competent, entry-level professional nurse generalist.
Apply critical thinking and clinical reasoning to form clinical judgments necessary for providing safe patient care and promoting quality improvement in a variety of health care settings.

Expand the use of nursing informatics and technology to effectively communicate, enhance knowledge, manage and analyze data, prevent errors, and support decision-making in preparation for becoming a competent, entry-level professional nurse generalist.
objectives: At the intermediate novice level: Quality, Safe, Patient-Centered Care A. Develop and implement a comprehensive patient-centered plan of care, using the nursing process, that addresses the psychosocial and physiological integrity, including health promotion and maintenance of acute and chronic health care needs in a variety of health care systems. B. Perform and document a patient-centered assessment for specific patient populations with complex health care needs encompassing values, preferences, expressed needs, and the impact of developmental, emotional, cultural, religious, and spiritual influences on the patient’s health status. C. Implement and document patient-centered health teaching interventions for patient populations with complex health care needs that address such topics as healthy lifestyles, risk-reducing behaviors, developmental needs, activities of daily living, and preventative self-care. D. Implement patient-centered care interventions that demonstrate sensitivity and respect for the diversity of the human experience. E. Investigate available resources and implement evidence-based practices to support clinical decision-making in the delivery of quality, safe nursing care. F. Safely perform psychomotor nursing skills, as outlined in the Nursing Skills Across the Curriculum, within the context of the patient situation. G. Demonstrate patient advocacy skills in the care of assigned patients with complex health care needs and their families.

Ethical and Legal Principles A. Embody professional standards, ethical behaviors, and legal principles in nursing practice. B. Model a positive image of nursing by embracing the values and articulating the knowledge, skills, and attitudes of the nursing profession. C. Embody professional attitudes and behaviors, including attention to appearance, demeanor, respect for self and others, and attention to professional boundaries with patients and families as well as caregivers. D. Demonstrate practice excellence, lifelong learning, and engagement in activities that foster professional growth and development in preparation for becoming a professional nurse generalist.

Leadership Principles A. Demonstrate effective use of organizational and time management skills to safely manage the complex health care needs of assigned patients. B. Assume a leadership role as a member of the health care team in a variety of patient care settings. C. Accept accountability and responsibility for nursing care of multiple patients with complex health care needs in a variety of settings, including licensed and unlicensed health care team members, in assigned or delegated tasks. D. Contribute to quality improvement processes to effectively implement patient safety initiatives and monitor performance outcomes.

Caring A. Incorporate interventions that address patient and family needs, including input from other health care team members when planning or providing care to patients with complex health care needs. B. Implement comprehensive nursing interventions that integrate the patient’s developmental level; physical and psychological needs; spiritual beliefs; and culture. C. Prioritize nursing care to facilitate the achievement of expected patient outcomes in a collaborative and caring manner that provides direction for continuity of care. D. Embody relationship-centered care behaviors for self-care and when interacting with patients, families, peers, and other members of the health care team.

Collaborative Relationships A. Demonstrate effective communication techniques to foster positive professional working relationships. B. Actively participate in collaborative relationships with the health care team, using appropriate communication skills, to improve patient outcomes and ensure the delivery of evidence-based patient-centered care. C. Prioritize and perform interventions that promote quality, safe patient-centered care as a member of the health care team that contributes to improving patient care outcomes. D. Analyze and document patient care data to inform the health care team and contribute to clinical decision-making. E. Prioritize and report relevant information to an appropriate health care team member to improve patient outcomes.

Critical Thinking A. Apply clinical reasoning and judgment skills in providing quality, safe patient-centered care to assigned patients. B. Individualize data collection, prioritize problems, establish goals, and select comprehensive interventions based on the patient’s immediate or anticipated needs of the patient and situation. C. Conduct ongoing evaluation of expected outcomes and interventions for patients with complex health care needs by analyzing assessment data to revise the individualized plan of care as needed. D. Engage in self-reflection and inquiry to examine professional learning needs. E. Implement quality improvement activities to prevent potential problems that may interfere with the delivery of safe patient care in a variety of health care settings.

Nursing Informatics A. Expand computer literacy, including the ability to use desktop applications and mobile technology to promote effective communication and support decision-making. B. Competently use patient care technologies, information systems, and mobile technology to support safe nursing care for assigned patients in a variety of health care settings. C. Proficiently use information technology systems to prevent the risk of errors and improve clinical outcomes in the delivery of safe patient care. D. Access relevant data and proficiently document using the nursing process via electronic health record, abiding by all ethical and legal standards.

outcomes: At the advanced beginner level, the student will: Provide quality, safe patient-centered basic nursing care using evidence-based practices for patients with complex alterations in health in preparation for becoming a competent, entry-level vocational nurse.

Function within the scope and standards of practice in preparation for becoming a competent, entry-level vocational nurse, applying ethical and legal principles, for patients with complex alterations in health.

rows.title: Introduction to Oceanography Laboratory
rows.title_printed: Course Outline: Riverside Community College District
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to demonstrate the following skills:
outcomes: Describe and explain the processes of plate tectonic theory, identify the major plates making up the earth's crust and explain how ocean basins are created and destroyed. With this knowledge, describe and illustrate on bathymetric maps the structure and features of ocean basins and explain how those features are created.

Perform a microscopic analysis of marine plankton and identify the different types and their abundances captured in seasonal plankton tows. Incorporate the analytical data with known seasonal variables such as nutrient levels, available sunlight and water temperature to synthesize a description of marine food chains and energy flow in marine ecosystems.

Preform macro- and microscopic analysis of marine rocks and sediments in order to discriminate between different types and develop an interpretation of the origin of the materials and the environments in which they form.

Predict both long- and short-term changes that could occur along a coastline from a given a set of oceanographic conditions such as tide, wave or storm track data. Explain what types of planning, preparation or construction should take place in order to accommodate the oceanographic conditions.

Plot buoy, drogue and satellite data including water temperature, salinity, wind direction, water speed and swell direction in order to determine what causes oceanic currents to form. Use the data to also determine where currents are located and the nature and characteristics of those currents.
objectives: Describe the scientific method as it applies to oceanographic phenomena.
Perform calculations using the metric system and produce graphs of oceanographic data.
Interpret charts of the seafloor in terms of plate tectonics and reconstruct tectonic boundaries on maps.
Identify major oceanic features from bathymetric maps.
Identify and interpret the origins and development of terrigenous and biogenous sediments.
Describe the density characteristics of water as controlled by temperature and salinity.
Compare and contrast processes that create wind-driven and density-driven current systems.
Describe processes of coastal erosion and relationship to rising sea-level and long-shore transport.
Describe major wave features, generation mechanisms, and seasonal distribution of wave types along coastlines.
Apply data from tide measurements and local weather to assess estuary processes.
Identify marine plankton taken from seasonal tows and calculate primary and secondary productivity.
Plot tracks and predict storm effects of hurricanes in the Caribbean, Gulf of Mexico and along Eastern U.S. seaboard states.
